facts.text: ISO 17757 is the safety standard for autonomous and semi-autonomous earth-moving and mining machine systems; ISO 19296 is the general safety standard for mobile machines working underground.
facts.quote: ISO 17757 is the safety standard for autonomous and semi-autonomous earth-moving and mining machine systems, and ISO 19296 is the general safety standard for mobile machines that work underground.

facts.text: ISO 17757:2019 is edition 2, confirmed, and applies to autonomous and semi-autonomous machine systems (ASAMS), including machines, infrastructure, hardware and software.
facts.quote: ISO 17757:2019 (edition 2, confirmed) applies to autonomous and semi-autonomous machine systems (ASAMS): machines, infrastructure, hardware and software.

facts.text: ISO 17757 requires safety-related parts of ASAMS control systems to meet appropriate functional safety performance.
facts.quote: It requires the safety-related parts of their control systems to meet appropriate functional safety performance

facts.text: ISO 17757 notes that electronic commands control brakes and steering on autonomous and semi-autonomous machines.
facts.quote: notes that electronic commands control brakes and steering on such machines

facts.text: ISO 17757 uses a "defined functional environment" within which an autonomous or semi-autonomous machine system is meant to operate.
facts.quote: uses the idea of a "defined functional environment" within which the system is meant to operate

facts.text: ISO 17757 braking and steering tests are physical tests run in manual and autonomous mode under ISO 3450 and ISO 10265.
facts.quote: Its braking and steering tests are physical, run in manual and autonomous mode under ISO 3450 and ISO 10265 [Chapter 10].

facts.text: Applicability of ISO 17757 to an isolated automatic-braking function on an operator-driven machine is unclear: function-specific automated features are outside its scope unless used as part of an ASAMS, so coverage should not automatically be claimed.
facts.quote: function-specific automated features are outside its scope unless used as part of an ASAMS, so "an isolated automatic-braking function on an operator-driven machine should not automatically be claimed to fall under it"

facts.text: No simulation wording was found in ISO 17757.
ISO 19296:2018 gives general safety and foreseeable-misuse requirements for mobile machines working underground.
facts.quote: ISO 19296:2018 gives general safety and foreseeable-misuse requirements for mobile machines working underground.

facts.text: ISO 21815-1 cites ISO 19296 to define the underground machines within its scope.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-1 cites it to define the underground machines in its scope

facts.text: ISO 19296 is not a stand-alone collision-avoidance performance protocol.
facts.quote: it is "not a stand-alone collision-avoidance performance protocol" [Chapter 3].

facts.text: For mining machines outside the ISO 6165 definition, ISO 19014 should not simply be assumed to apply; ISO 19296 and generic standards may apply by contract or jurisdiction.
facts.quote: For mining machines outside the ISO 6165 definition, ISO 19014 should not simply be assumed to apply; ISO 19296 and generic standards may apply by contract or jurisdiction [Chapter 3].

facts.text: An operator-driven machine with an intervention function sits in a gray zone between ISO 21815 collision avoidance and ISO 17757 autonomy; the booklet identifies this as an open uncertainty.
facts.quote: An operator-driven machine with an intervention function sits in a gray zone between ISO 21815 (collision avoidance) and ISO 17757 (autonomy). The booklet lists this among its open uncertainties

facts.text: Applicable standards for the operator-driven machine intervention function should be settled early by a qualified functional-safety specialist.
facts.quote: asks that applicable standards be settled early by a qualified functional-safety specialist [Chapters 3, 12].

facts.text: ISO 17757's "defined functional environment" corresponds to the operational design domain concept used for staged release in the off-road program.
facts.quote: ISO 17757's "defined functional environment" is the off-road cousin of the operational design domain used for staged release [Chapter 1].
